cultural.vision_reason: This is a large embroidered wide-sleeved gown (boubou/tobe/riga) of the type worn across the Western Sudan region including by Wolof men, made of machine-woven strip cloth with hand-embroidered pocket and roundel motifs typical of this dress tradition.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (boubou, tobe, riga: part of a three-piece costume, with trousers and shirt, Af1984,07.1 to 3). Composed of 18 wide strips of blue machine-made cotton with the same damask pattern as in Af1984,07.1, which have been machine-sewn together. The body of the gown has the strips sewn vertically; the arms are sewn horizontally. A square ‘pocket’ has been added at the front, over which has been sewn by hand in a light blue cotton embroidery in the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern. On the breast are two circles, with a smaller one on the back. The gown has been lined in white machine-woven cotton behind the areas of embroidery and along the inside of the bottom hem.
